answer: Behavioral plume tracing: each identity carries a persistent behavioral signature (timing, phrasing, tool-call sequences) captured at registration and re-checked on every action. Duplicates show correlated signatures against a shared anchor of reference actions, so a copied agent's first few outputs already expose the overlap. Any identity whose signature mirrors another's within tolerance is flagged and suspended pending manual review, and the operator must re-derive a fresh signature from scratch, costing roughly 40 hours of genuine interaction per new identity.
